learned: SNMP is UDP; a plain tsh ssh -L port-forward is TCP-only and cannot carry it -- a UDP<->TCP relay is required on both ends of a Teleport tunnel for any SNMP-over-Teleport use case, not just this one. LibreNMS 2024+ images no longer ship the classic addhost.php script; use lnms device:add / lnms device:poll instead. The mariadb:11.4 image used for librenms-db needs mariadbd not mysqld in its Compose command and has no mysql client alias, only mariadb.

assumption: D3+D7+D8 -- the platform/config/abstraction knot -- can be settled by more analysis (external per-layer review of the options register, further decision enumeration) rather than by running T6, the two-shim test, against the real adapter surface.
killed: Nothing in the design, which is the point -- the disconfirming outcome did not occur. What it killed is the premise the RED named: that the knot needed more analysis first. T6 ran 2026-09-21 against the live XV2 field contract captured 2026-09-20 (hope-vale, firmware 6.6.0.3-r9). Shim A, DeviceObservation to NetJSON DeviceMonitoring for the OpenWISP monitoring endpoint: 97 code lines, 168 total. Shim B, observation split into durable inventory objects plus timestamped line-protocol samples: 111 code lines, 156 total. Threshold was roughly 300 lines each; neither came close. Criterion 2 checked mechanically -- 75 protocol identifiers parsed out of protocol.py with ast and matched against a framework-noun list (netjson, openwisp, nautobot, dcim, influx, prometheus, htmode, mfp, wmm, wds and others); zero hits. The pass-through backend premise that the whole OpenWISP recommendation rests on therefore survives its own named test, and the D3.6 hybrid is not forced by shim cost. NetJSON schema was verified from primary source this run (openwisp_monitoring/device/schema.py on master), not from memory.
learned: Three things the test surfaced that the analysis rounds had not. FIRST, the design record's claim that the enterprise Wi-Fi family maps cleanly onto NetJSON is true for the wireless interface object and FALSE for the client object. NetJSON requires seven client fields (auth, authorized, ht, vht, wmm, mac, mfp); the Cambium contract reports only mac and authorized, ht and vht are derivable from the client mode string, auth is weakly inferable, and wmm and mfp are neither reported nor derivable. Shim A fabricates those two visibly via a named constant rather than silently defaulting them, because a silent default is indistinguishable from a measurement once it reaches a dashboard. This does not trip T6 -- the distortion is absorbed in the shim and never reaches the protocol -- but it means per-client telemetry through OpenWISP carries two columns that are not measurements, which is direct evidence for D6 and for the unanswered operator question about whether per-client identity is needed at all. SECOND, writing shim A forced exactly one protocol field: DeviceIdentity.country_code, because the NetJSON wireless object requires country. Kept rather than shimmed around because regulatory domain is a genuine device fact the hardware reports natively and one any RF-managing controller wants regardless of platform; recorded beside the field so the judgement is reviewable. A shim asking for a field is the moment to check whether it earns its place off-platform. THIRD, running the adapter against real values caught a unit error the schema alone would not have: memory was modelled as memory_used_bytes but the device returns 44 beside cpu 6, so it is a percentage. Renamed, with the inference and its residual uncertainty stated. Residual: no live round-trip yet, the backfill timestamp format is unverified and belongs to the pull-path test, and only one family on one firmware is covered -- the design record's warning that point-to-multipoint and 60GHz mesh do NOT map cleanly onto NetJSON is still untested.
